title: PRD: Optimize – “Increase cache hit-rate” recommendations (MVP)
author: Aditya Rao
body:
## Summary
Optimize will ship a first-pass recommendation experience that uses KV/prefix cache telemetry (v2) to suggest concrete actions customers can take to increase cache effectiveness and reduce prefill latency/cost.

This PRD defines the MVP user experience, recommendation types, success metrics, guardrails, and rollout plan.

## Background / Why now
Customers regularly ask, “Is my cache working?” and “What should I do to improve hit-rate?” Today we provide raw metrics/dashboards, but not actionable guidance. Meanwhile, the cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint is adding trustworthy telemetry (hit/miss/partial, hit-bytes, saved-prefill-ms, cacheable prompt ratio) with consistent attribution tags. This unlocks an Optimize feature that:
- Converts telemetry into prioritized actions.
- Reduces time-to-diagnosis for performance/cost issues.
- Improves customer outcomes without requiring deep cache expertise.

## Problem statement
Even when caching is enabled, customers frequently experience:
- Low hit-rate due to prompt/prefix variability.
- Fragmented routing (multiple routes/models/versions) preventing reuse.
- Cache policy misconfiguration (TTL/size/eviction) that limits effective reuse.
- Confusing or misleading signals (partial-prefill, retries, streaming behavior) that obscure whether the cache is helping.

Customers need a concise, evidence-backed list of “next best actions” tied to their routes/models.

## Goals (MVP)
1) Provide a ranked set of recommendations that a customer can act on to improve cache effectiveness.
2) Each recommendation must include: what’s happening, why it matters, what to change, and evidence (metrics + scope).
3) Drive measurable improvements in cache outcomes for a subset of workloads (targeted uplift rather than broad averages).
4) Reduce support burden by proactively answering common cache tuning questions.

## Non-goals (MVP)
- A fully ML-driven recommendation engine or automated prompt rewriting.
- Automatically changing customer routing/policies (we only recommend; customer opts in).
- UI polish beyond a basic “Recommendations feed” and supporting detail drawer.
- Perfect root-cause classification for all edge cases (we will have explicit data sufficiency checks and “cannot determine” states).

## Target users / Personas
Primary:
- **ML Engineer / Applied ML (customer):** Wants lower latency and cost; can change prompts/templates.
- **Platform / Infra Engineer (customer):** Owns routes, model selection, deployments, caching policies.

Secondary:
- **SRE / On-call (customer):** Needs quick diagnostics when performance regresses.
- **Redwood CSM / Support:** Uses recommendations as a consistent narrative + checklist during escalations.

## User stories
1) As a platform engineer, I want to see which routes have the worst cache effectiveness and what to change first.
2) As an ML engineer, I want guidance on how to structure prompts to increase shared prefixes without harming output quality.
3) As an SRE, I want to know whether a hit-rate drop is due to traffic mix/routing fragmentation vs cache eviction/policy issues.
4) As a support engineer, I want evidence links (dashboards/metrics) so I can validate recommendations quickly.

## User experience (MVP)
### Entry points
- **Redwood Console → Optimize → Recommendations → “Cache hit-rate”** (new category filter)
- Optional: contextual entry from cache hit-rate dashboard panel (“View recommendations for this route”).

### Feed behavior
- Shows top N (default 10) active recommendations for selected scope (Org / Project / Route).
- Sort order: severity/impact (estimated savings) then confidence.
- Each item has: title, impacted scope, estimated impact, confidence, last evaluated timestamp.
- Click opens a detail drawer with:
  - Evidence summary (metrics + time window)
  - “Why this happens”
  - “What to do next” (step-by-step)
  - Links: relevant dashboards, docs, and (when available) route config pages

### Actions
- **Dismiss** (with reason): “Not applicable”, “Already fixed”, “Will not fix”, “Need more data”.
- **Snooze** for X days.
- **Mark as done** (optional) to track adoption.

### Data freshness
- MVP evaluation runs **hourly** on aggregated telemetry.
- UI displays “Last computed: <timestamp>” and “Data window: last 24h (default)”.

## Recommendation types (MVP scope)
The MVP will implement a small set of high-signal heuristics.

For each type, we define: trigger, evidence, suggested actions, and guardrails.

### R1: Prompt prefix variability (low cacheable prefix reuse)
**Symptom:** Cacheable prompt ratio is reasonable, but hit-rate remains low; high prefix diversity for a route/model.

**Trigger (example):**
- cacheable_prompt_ratio >= 0.30
- cache_hit_rate < 0.20
- prefix_diversity_index above threshold (see Telemetry Inputs)
- Min volume: >= 5k requests / 24h (configurable)

**Suggested actions:**
- Normalize prompts: move dynamic fields (timestamps, UUIDs, user-specific metadata) later in the prompt.
- Template stabilization: enforce consistent system prefix; canonicalize whitespace; stable ordering of instructions.
- For tool/function calling: keep tool schema and instructions stable; avoid injecting variable debug info early.

**Evidence shown:**
- Route/model scope
- cache_hit_rate, cacheable_prompt_ratio
- “Top prefix clusters cover X% of traffic” (bucketed/hashed; no raw text)

**Guardrails:**
- Never display raw prompt content. Only show hashed prefix buckets and aggregate shares.
- Do not recommend normalization if cacheable_prompt_ratio is low (see R4).

### R2: Routing fragmentation (requests split across routes/regions/models)
**Symptom:** Similar traffic is distributed across multiple route IDs, model versions, or regions, preventing cache reuse.

**Trigger (example):**
- Route group (customer-defined or inferred) spans >= 3 routes or >= 2 model versions
- Fragmentation index high and hit-rate low relative to expected baseline
- Min volume: >= 10k requests / 24h

**Suggested actions:**
- Consolidate to fewer routes for the same workload.
- Pin model version for stable reuse (especially for Dedicated pools).
- Prefer consistent region selection where feasible; reduce cross-region fanout for cache-sensitive traffic.

**Evidence shown:**
- Share of traffic by route/model_version/region
- Hit-rate per route/model_version (top 5)

**Guardrails:**
- Only suggest model pinning if customer has configured rollouts compatible with pinning (or we can phrase as “consider pinning”).
- Avoid recommendations that conflict with availability/failover policies; include “tradeoff” note.

### R3: Cache policy mismatch (TTL/size/eviction pressure)
**Symptom:** Hit-rate is unstable; high eviction rate; saved-prefill-ms is lower than expected given cacheable prompt ratio.

**Trigger (example):**
- Eviction events per 1k requests above threshold
- Cache miss rate spikes correlate with elevated evictions
- Cacheable prompts present (cacheable_prompt_ratio >= 0.25)

**Suggested actions:**
- Increase cache capacity (if dedicated/private) or adjust per-tenant cache allocation.
- Adjust TTL to better match request repetition intervals.
- Reduce routing fragmentation (links to R2) if cache is being diluted.

**Evidence shown:**
- Eviction rate trend and correlation with hit-rate
- saved_prefill_ms trend (p50/p95)

**Guardrails:**
- Hosted customers may not have direct cache sizing controls; copy must switch to “contact support / enable Dedicated cache controls” or “optimize prompt reuse first”.

### R4: Low cacheable prompt ratio (workload not structured for caching)
**Symptom:** Most requests are not cacheable (e.g., minimal stable prefix, highly variable system instructions).

**Trigger (example):**
- cacheable_prompt_ratio < 0.10
- Min volume: >= 5k requests / 24h

**Suggested actions:**
- Introduce stable system prefix; keep policies/instructions consistent.
- Move volatile context to later turns; avoid re-sending large, changing system blocks.
- Consider separating routes: one for stable instruction prefix, one for ad-hoc prompts.

**Evidence shown:**
- cacheable_prompt_ratio and how it compares to org median

**Guardrails:**
- If route is intentionally unique prompts (e.g., “free-form playground”), allow easy dismissal with “Not applicable”.

### R5 (Optional stretch): Partial-prefill / streaming retry skew warning
**Symptom:** hit-rate appears high but saved-prefill-ms is low (or vice versa), suggesting partial-prefill counting or retry behavior is skewing results.

**Trigger (example):**
- cache_hit_rate and saved_prefill_ms are inconsistent beyond tolerance
- High retry rate / streaming reconnect indicators (if available)

**Outcome:**
- Show as “Data interpretation warning” rather than an “action” recommendation.

**Guardrails:**
- Must link to known-issues page and recommend verifying telemetry version/flag status.

## Telemetry inputs (minimum required)
MVP requires the following v2 telemetry availability (aggregated at route/model/version/region/deployment_mode, within cardinality budgets):
- cache_hit_rate (by outcome: hit/miss/partial)
- cache_hit_bytes
- saved_prefill_ms (estimated) and/or saved_prefill_tokens (if available)
- cacheable_prompt_ratio
- cache_evictions (count / rate)
- Request volume (requests, tokens)
- Attribution tags: tenant_id (coarse), route_id, model, model_version, region, deployment_mode

Derived features (computed in analytics job; must be non-PII):
- prefix_diversity_index (based on hashed prefix buckets)
- routing_fragmentation_index (distribution entropy across route/model_version/region)
- stability indicators (variance of hit-rate day-over-day)

Data sufficiency rules:
- Recommendations require a minimum request count and a minimum evaluation window (default last 24h).
- If sampling is enabled, apply sampling-aware confidence adjustments.

## Recommendation object requirements (API + storage)
The backend will persist computed recommendations to support:
- Stable IDs (dedupe across runs)
- Dismissal/snooze state
- Auditability (what evidence produced the recommendation)

Required fields (conceptual):
- recommendation_id, type, title
- scope (tenant/project/route/model/version/region)
- severity (P0–P3) and confidence (low/med/high)
- estimated_impact (e.g., “~8–15% prefill time reduction”)
- evidence: metric deltas + time window + dashboard links
- created_at, last_evaluated_at, expires_at
- user_state: open/dismissed/snoozed/done + reason

Note: exact field names are defined in the Recommendations Feed API contract doc.

## Success metrics
### Product outcomes
- **Adoption:** % of active orgs viewing Cache recommendations at least once per week.
- **Engagement:** Average recommendations opened per session; dismissal vs “mark done” rates.
- **Actionability:** % of recommendations that are not dismissed as “Not applicable” (target: >= 60% in beta cohorts).

### Technical outcomes
Measured on routes/orgs where a recommendation was acted upon (self-reported “done” and/or observed config changes when detectable):
- **Hit-rate uplift:** +5–10 absolute points on affected routes within 14 days (goal is directional; varies by workload).
- **Saved prefill improvement:** measurable increase in saved_prefill_ms or decrease in p95 prefill latency.
- **Support deflection:** reduction in cache-metric confusion tickets (baseline from support queue; target TBD).

### Quality / Safety metrics
- False-positive rate (customer dismisses as “Incorrect”) < 10% in beta cohorts.
- No P0 incidents caused by recommendation evaluation jobs or UI (availability and latency budgets).

## Guardrails & constraints
1) **No prompt leakage:** Never store or display raw prompt content. Use hashed buckets and only show aggregate shares.
2) **Cardinality controls:** Recommendations must operate on aggregated dimensions within ADR-027 limits; no per-request identifiers.
3) **Data sufficiency:** If data is missing, heavily sampled, or telemetry flags are partially enabled, do not generate high-confidence recommendations.
4) **Don’t break reliability:** Recommendations must not encourage disabling failover/routing safety. When suggesting pinning/consolidation, include tradeoff notes and “validate with canary”.
5) **Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private:** Copy and available actions must reflect what controls the customer actually has.
6) **Known issues awareness:** If a route matches known skew patterns (streaming retries/partial-prefill), show a warning and link to troubleshooting instead of confident “fix” advice.

## Dependencies
- KV cache telemetry v2 spec + runtime instrumentation and gateway attribution (feature flagged).
- Analytics job to compute derived indices and rank recommendations.
- Console Recommendations feed backend endpoint + UI.
- Dashboards/links for evidence validation (SRE/Telemetry owned).

## Risks
- **Misleading recommendations from telemetry gaps:** mitigated via sufficiency checks, confidence levels, and warnings.
- **Customer confusion between hit-rate and savings:** mitigated via consistent copy emphasizing saved_prefill_ms/hit-bytes and “what good looks like”.
- **Overhead / pipeline lag:** mitigated via staged rollout and ability to disable recommendation generation independently.
- **Actionability varies by workload:** mitigated by focusing MVP on top 3–4 high-signal patterns and explicit “Not applicable” paths.

## Rollout plan
### Phase 0: Internal dogfood (Redwood-only)
- Enable for Redwood internal tenants in 1–2 regions.
- Validate recommendation correctness against manual investigations.
- Add logging for “why generated / why suppressed” (internal only).

### Phase 1: Limited beta (opt-in)
- Select 5–10 design partners (mix of Hosted + Dedicated).
- Weekly review with Support/CSM; track false positives and copy clarity.
- Iterate thresholds and ranking.

### Phase 2: Broad beta (tier-gated)
- Default on for Dedicated customers and Hosted customers above a traffic threshold.
- Add basic in-product feedback: “Helpful / Not helpful”.

### Phase 3: GA
- Enable by default for all tenants where telemetry v2 is enabled.
- Publish customer-facing docs: “Improving cache hit-rate” including examples.

Feature flags:
- telemetry.kv_cache.v2_enabled (data collection)
- optimize.cache_recommendations.enabled (recommendation generation + UI)

## Open questions
1) Ranking: do we prioritize by estimated saved_prefill_ms, by cost impact, or by “likelihood of actionability”? (Proposal: saved_prefill_ms primary; fall back to hit-rate delta potential.)
2) How do we detect that a customer “took action” without deep integration into routing/config systems? (MVP: user-marked “done” + optional heuristics.)
3) What is the minimum viable “evidence link” format across Hosted/Dedicated/Private dashboards?
4) Should we support per-project scoping in MVP, or only org + route?

## Appendix: Copy guidance (MVP tone)
- Be explicit about confidence and data window.
- Use actionable verbs (“Consolidate routes”, “Pin model version”, “Move dynamic fields later”).
- Avoid implying guarantees; use ranges and suggest validating with canary.
- Always include a “Why this happens” explanation to teach cache mental models.
